faq.question: What is an AI API router?
faq.answer: An AI API router is a single endpoint that forwards your requests to many AI model providers. Instead of integrating OpenAI, Anthropic and Google separately, you call one OpenAI-compatible API and the router dispatches each request to the right model.

faq.question: Is MuiRouter the same as Material UI?
faq.answer: No. MuiRouter is an AI/LLM API router for language models — unrelated to the Material UI (MUI) React component library. The name comes from the muirouter.com domain.

faq.question: Which models can I route to?
faq.answer: OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, xAI Grok, Cloudflare Workers AI and Xiaomi MiMo today, with more added over time. You can start free on MiMo and top up for the rest.

faq.question: Do I need a VPN or an overseas account?
faq.answer: No. MuiRouter is proxied through Cloudflare's global edge network, so you can reach every provider without a VPN or a foreign credit card.

aiRouter.ctaDescription: Create a free account, grab an API key, and point your OpenAI SDK at MuiRouter.

faq.question: What is an LLM router?
faq.answer: An LLM router is a gateway that sends your prompts to different large language models through one interface. It lets you compare, switch or combine models like GPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok without rewriting your integration.

faq.question: How do I switch between models?
faq.answer: Keep the same OpenAI-compatible request and change the model field — for example from a GPT model to a Claude or Gemini model. MuiRouter routes it to the right provider.

faq.question: Can I use my existing OpenAI code?
faq.answer: Yes. MuiRouter is OpenAI-compatible, so you only change the Base URL and API key. See the OpenAI-compatible router page for details.

faq.question: What does OpenAI-compatible mean?
faq.answer: It means MuiRouter accepts the same request and response format as the OpenAI API. Any client built for OpenAI can talk to MuiRouter by changing only the Base URL and API key.

faq.question: Is MuiRouter cheaper than OpenRouter?
faq.answer: It depends on your usage pattern. MuiRouter's per-token price already includes the platform's cost, with no separate fee on adding funds. OpenRouter passes through provider pricing with no token markup, but charges 5.5% on credit-card top-ups (5% on crypto) and 5% on BYOK usage past the free monthly allowance. Compare exact per-model rates on the pricing page.

faq.question: Does MuiRouter support as many models as OpenRouter?
faq.answer: No — MuiRouter is a curated set of OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Workers AI, Moonshot and MiMo models, while OpenRouter's catalog spans hundreds of models across dozens of providers. If you need a handful of mainstream providers with native endpoint access, MuiRouter is narrower but deeper; if you need long-tail model variety, OpenRouter has more breadth.

faq.question: Can I switch from OpenRouter to MuiRouter without rewriting my code?
faq.answer: Yes. Both are OpenAI-compatible, so for standard chat completions you only change the Base URL and API key. Provider-specific request options may need small adjustments — check the OpenAI-compatible router page for details.

faq.question: Is LiteLLM free?
faq.answer: The open-source core (Python SDK and Proxy Server) is free and self-hosted — you run the infrastructure. LiteLLM Enterprise adds SSO/SCIM, audit logs and 24/7 support for production teams, priced through their sales team.

faq.question: Do I need to run my own server with OpenRouter or MuiRouter?
faq.answer: No. Both OpenRouter and MuiRouter are managed — you get an API key and call the endpoint, with no proxy to deploy or maintain. That's the main practical difference from LiteLLM's self-hosted model.

faq.question: Which one should I use?
faq.answer: If you want full control, custom routing logic and no per-request platform fee, self-hosting LiteLLM makes sense. If you want a managed endpoint with the widest model catalog, OpenRouter fits. If you want a managed endpoint with native Claude/GPT access and no separate top-up fee, try MuiRouter.

faq.question: Is MuiRouter related to Material UI (MUI)?
faq.answer: No. MuiRouter is an OpenAI-compatible AI/LLM API router and MCP server, named after the muirouter.com domain. It has nothing to do with the Material UI (MUI) React component library or MUI X.

faq.question: What is MuiRouter?
faq.answer: MuiRouter is an AI API router: one key routes your requests to OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, xAI Grok, Cloudflare Workers AI and Xiaomi MiMo, billed per token with no subscription.

faq.question: Is it OpenAI-compatible?
faq.answer: Yes. Point the OpenAI SDK's Base URL at MuiRouter and keep your existing code. See the OpenAI-compatible router page to learn more.

faq.question: Can I use Claude Code or the Anthropic SDK with MuiRouter?
faq.answer: Yes. MuiRouter exposes a native Anthropic /v1/messages endpoint. Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to MuiRouter and use your sk-gw- key — Claude Code, the Anthropic SDK and any Anthropic-native client run on your MuiRouter balance, with no Anthropic account required.

mcpPage.title: MCP integration guide
mcpPage.intro: MuiRouter runs a streamable-HTTP MCP server so AI clients like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and Cline can call it directly — your AI assistant can check your balance, view usage, list models, generate images and even start a top-up. Everything is authenticated with your own sk-gw- API key, so neither third parties nor AI clients need a new account.
mcpPage.endpointDesc: All MCP clients connect to the same URL using Bearer auth.
mcpPage.protocolNote: Protocol version: MCP 2025-06-18, transport: streamable-http, stateless JSON-RPC 2.0.
mcpPage.claudeCodeDesc: Edit ~/.claude/mcp.json and add the muirouter server.
mcpPage.claudeCodeNote: After restarting Claude Code, type /mcp to see the muirouter tool list.
mcpPage.clientsDesc: Fill in the same URL and Authorization header.
mcpPage.cursorDesc: Cursor: Settings → MCP → Add new server, choose the streamable-http type, set the URL to {url}, and add a custom header {header}.
mcpPage.claudeDesktopDesc: Claude Desktop: edit the config file (macOS: {path}) with the same configuration as Claude Code above.
mcpPage.toolsDesc: Six tools covering account queries, pricing, image generation and top-ups.

tools.get_balance: Query the wallet balance, total top-ups and total spending for the user that owns the current API key.
tools.get_usage: Paginate through the current user's API usage, filterable by model and time range.
tools.list_recharges: Paginate through the current user's top-up records.
tools.list_models: List every model MuiRouter currently supports and its pricing (input/output, markup_rate).
tools.create_topup_session: Create a Stripe top-up session and return a payment link the AI client can guide the user through.
tools.image_generation: Call the OpenAI-compatible image generation endpoint through MuiRouter (consumes wallet balance).

mcpPage.jsonRpcDesc: You can also call it directly with curl, without an MCP client.
mcpPage.security1: Your API key is like a password — never expose it in a public repository or chat log. If you suspect it leaked, revoke it immediately on the Keys page.
mcpPage.security2: image_generation and create_topup_session spend or move money. Consider setting these two tools to require confirmation in your AI client.
mcpPage.security3: Every request is tied to the account behind its sk-gw- key, with the same concurrency and billing rules as calling the REST API directly.
